subject: Compliance sprint: scope triage for FedRAMP path + ISO checkpoints
messages:
From: Jordan Harris <jordan.harris@acmebank.com>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: audit-ops@acmebank.com
Date: Thu, 02 Sep 2026 14:08:00 -0700
Subject: Compliance sprint: FedRAMP scoping and ISO considerations

Hi Lukas / team,

Thanks for taking this on. We are putting together our FedRAMP-ready procurement packet and want to validate scope tradeoffs before the formal RFP. A few items we need clarified from Redwood: 

- Which control families you expect to keep in-scope for a FedRAMP Moderate deployment vs. the baseline ISO27001 boundary (particularly A.9 / A.12 / A.14).
- Evidence cadence: what snapshot windows (daily / weekly / 30d logs) you can provide for log sampling and how you surface those artifacts.
- Who would be the primary evidence owners on Redwood's side for KMS/snapshot exports and for runtime network segmentation logs.
- Whether you can provide a SIG/CAIQ pre-populated matrix for our procurement team — we can accept high-level narratives if a full artifact is not immediate.

We also attached a short questionnaire matrix with our priority asks (see redwood-questionnaire-matrix.xlsx). Can we schedule a 30-minute triage session early next week to align owners and cutoff windows? Ideally before our internal security review on 2026-09-15.

Thanks,
Jordan
Jordan Harris
Senior Security Engineer — Acme Bank
Jordan.harris@acmebank.com

Attachment: redwood-questionnaire-matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Harris <jordan.harris@acmebank.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 03 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Compliance sprint: FedRAMP scoping and ISO considerations

Hi Jordan — thanks for the clear list. Quick take and proposed next steps below.

Scope tradeoffs
- For a Moderate FedRAMP profile we anticipate keeping the same service boundary as our standard Private deployment but expanding evidence collection for some control families (notably logging retention and KMS attestations). ISO scope mapping (Annex A) is close to a 1:1 fit for many controls; A.9 (access) and A.12 (operations) will require the most evidence work.

Evidence cadence
- Log snapshots: we can provide daily rolling log exports for the past 30 days and weekly aggregated snapshots for 12 months. We also produce on-demand point-in-time snapshots for audit sampling.
- Crypto/KMS: we can provide KMS usage reports and key rotation logs; HSM attestation material may be available via our private deployment offering (we'll enumerate what is included in hosted vs. dedicated vs. private).

Owners and attachments
- Proposed owners: Kimberly will own KMS/key evidence and Marissa will own audit artifacts for logging & traceability. I'm including a control mapping draft (control-mapping.pdf) to show how we map common SIG questions to evidence types. 

Next steps
1) Quick triage call: propose Mon 2026-09-06 10:00 PT (30m) — please confirm.
2) Kimberly/Marissa to attach owner artifacts after call (KMS mapping, snapshot playbook).
3) We'll produce a trimmed SIG/CAIQ extract that highlights where we can provide native artifacts vs. narrative answers.

If you need a formal NDA or a secure upload channel for sensitive artifacts, let us know and we can provide a presigned S3 link or use your secure portal.

Best,
Lukas Meyer
Head of Compliance Outreach — Redwood Inference
lukas_meyer@redwood.com

Attachment: control-mapping.pdf (PDF stub)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwood.com>, Jordan Harris <jordan.harris@acmebank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 06 Sep 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Compliance sprint: FedRAMP scoping and ISO considerations

On Fri, 03 Sep 2026 at 09:12 AM Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwood.com> wrote:
> Proposed owners: Kimberly will own KMS/key evidence and Marissa will own audit artifacts for logging & traceability.

Confirmed — I'll take KMS and crypto-level artifacts. Notes: 
- I will provide a KMS ownership spreadsheet (kms_ownership.xlsx) that maps key aliases to control narratives and rotation records.
- HSM attestation: for customers on Redwood Private we can include HSM / HSM-backed key attestations; for hosted customers we provide KMS usage logs and rotation history only.
- For FedRAMP Moderate customers we recommend a dedicated key-per-tenant approach — we can document the tradeoffs (operational overhead vs. audit simplicity).

Jordan — happy to include a short extract of rotation logs to help your auditors evaluate frequency and access controls. Will upload to the Drive folder Lukas linked after our call.

Kimberly Park
Senior Security Engineer — Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com

Attachment: kms_ownership.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: Jordan Harris <jordan.harris@acmebank.com>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, audit-ops@acmebank.com
Date: Tue, 08 Sep 2026 09:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Compliance sprint: FedRAMP scoping and ISO considerations

Thanks all — Monday at 10:00 PT works for us. Couple quick clarifications ahead of the call: 

- Can you confirm whether your daily log snapshots will include request‑level IP and user agent fields (we need those for multiple A.12 controls)?
- For ISO, our team would like a short mapping to Annex A controls for A.9 (Access control), A.12 (Operations) and A.14 (Development). Narrative is fine as long as you cite artifact types.

If you can upload the KMS spreadsheet and the draft control mapping to the Drive link before the call that would be ideal. See you Monday.

—Jordan
Jordan Harris
Senior Security Engineer — Acme Bank
jordan.harris@acmebank.com

Attachment: none
